papers.title_in_file: Speeding up quantum perceptron via shortcuts to adiabaticity
papers.version_note: arXiv:2003.09938v3 (22 Aug 2021). The text layer holds the main article with Methods (pages 1 to 7) and the Supplemental Material (pages 8 and 9). A first-version-like title block with garbled figure markup is embedded on page 2; the text layer lost parts of Eq. (4), Eq. (8) and the Hadamard-gate sentence (square-root signs), and some lines of the page 5 and page 8 text are interleaved.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical proposal that designs, by invariant-based inverse engineering of a shortcut to adiabaticity, a control field for a single-qubit quantum perceptron so that its excitation probability gives a sigmoid activation function in a shorter operation time than the FAQUAD protocol.

existing.note: The abstract claims faster performance and enhanced robustness against imperfections in the controls. The body supports the speed claim with minimum operation times (0.2 for the cubic ansatz and 0.15 for the fifth-order ansatz against 0.3 for FAQUAD). The only robustness result in the body is robustness to variations in the operation time t f (timing errors); insensitivity to the kappa parameter is also shown. No other control imperfection (amplitude noise, detuning, decoherence) is simulated.
existing.value: The authors propose a quantum perceptron in which a control field is inversely engineered, giving a rapid nonlinear response with a sigmoid activation function, and report faster overall performance than quasi-adiabatic protocols; the robustness shown in the body is to timing errors, that is, variations on the operation time t f.

assertions.value: The authors state that by increasing the value of xmax, which means more energy is supplied to the system, a more stretched sigmoid can be recovered with the FAQUAD protocol or with IE and the polynomial ansatz of N = 3, and that their work instead finds the driving for a fixed Hamiltonian configuration with the range [−xmax, xmax].

we ﬁnd the external driving Ω(t) by which the perceptron can have a sigmoidal response in a ﬁxed Hamiltonian conﬁguration with the range [−xmax, xmax].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of the scope of its comparison; the recovery for larger xmax is stated without a plot.
assertions.reader_inference: The speed-up over FAQUAD is therefore tied to the fixed range xmax = 12; the paper shows no comparison at other ranges.

assertions.value: The authors state that the controls Ω(t) derived from IE are smooth and present values close to zero at t = 0, in contrast with the FAQUAD controls, which demand an abrupt change from Ω(0) = 2000 to Ω(t f ) = 1, and they conclude that this shows the appropriateness of the IE controls for experimental implementation.
quotes: the derived controls Ω(t) from IE methods are smooth and present values close to zero at t = 0
demands an abrupt change from Ω(0) = 2000 to Ω(t f ) = 1
This demonstrates the appropriateness of our IE derived controls to be implemented experimentally.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical (numerical) observation plus an author claim of experimental suitability.
assertions.reader_inference: The suitability is argued from plotted controls and parameter estimates, not tested in an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the FAQUAD protocol keeps the adiabatic parameter constant, µ(t) = c, during the whole control process, and that the largest value of |µ| occurs at |x j/Ω f | ≈ 1.272, which they take as the optimal condition that works for all input neuron configurations.

assertions.reader_inference: The FAQUAD baseline is the authors' own implementation, tuned at one worst-case point, not an independently optimized baseline.

assertions.value: The authors tabulate, for t f = 0.15, xmax = 12 and y/Ω f = 12, P(−xmax), P(xmax) and C for polynomial, trigonometric and exponential ansatz and for FAQUAD; the FAQUAD row reads 0.204 0.796 0.41, and the polynomial rows read 0.204 0.998 0.206, 0.024 0.998 0.026 and 0.0065 0.998 0.008.
quotes: Comparison of the performance of diﬀerent ansatz: polynomial, trigonometric and exponential functions in form introduced in the main text, with t f = 0.15, xmax = 12, y/Ω f = 12.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical (numerical) result from one study, read from a table.
assertions.reader_inference: The polynomial rows are in order of increasing polynomial order (three, four, five). In the trigonometric row of order four, C is listed as 0.0389 although P(−xmax) is 0.0429, so C should be at least that large; this looks like a table error.

assertions.value: The paper states, citing Cybenko, that the universal approximation theorem claims that any continuous function can be written as a linear combination of sigmoid functions, and that a quantum neural network is also demonstrated as a universal approximator of continuous functions (citing other work).
quotes: “universal approximation theorem” proved by Cybenko [43], claiming that any continuous function can be written as a linear combination of sigmoid func-
A QNN is also demonstrated as a universal approxi-
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result attributed to other work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's gloss of Cybenko's theorem is loose (the theorem concerns uniform approximation by finite sums of sigmoids on compact sets).

assertions.value: The paper states that a universal quantum perceptron has been proposed as an efficient approximator in earlier work, where the quantum perceptron is encoded in an Ising model with a sigmoid activation function, and that a quantum algorithm for a binary-valued perceptron was introduced in other earlier work, showing an exponential advantage in resources storage.
quotes: showing an exponential advantage in resources storage.
a universal quantum perceptron has been proposed as an eﬃcient approximator in Ref. [34]
the quantum perceptron is encoded in an Ising model with a sigmoid activation function.
assertions.certainty_reason: Results the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate that their method produces solutions that outperform those based on adiabatic techniques, which significantly facilitates the implementation of quantum perceptrons in modern platforms such as nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond.
quotes: We demonstrate that our method produces solutions that outperform those based on adiabatic techniques
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the supporting numerical results are entered separately.
assertions.reader_inference: The baseline is FAQUAD (a fast quasi-adiabatic protocol) from the same group's earlier work, not a general adiabatic baseline.
